description: Composite figure combining SEM micrographs and EDS elemental maps of a plasma rotating electrode process (PREP) powder with nominal composition Fe–30Mn–9Al–C–3Ni. (a) is a low-magnification SEM image of a large powder bed (printed scale bar 400 μm) in which essentially all particles are spherical and closely size-matched, with no satellites or irregular fragments; a dashed white box marks the particle enlarged in (b), a high-magnification SEM view (printed scale bar 10 μm) whose surface is smooth but faintly granular/faceted. (c)–(f) are EDS maps of the same particle field, colour-coded and labelled in the top-right corner: (c) yellow "Fe", (d) blue "Mn", (e) red "Al", (f) magenta "Ni"; every element is distributed evenly across the mapped particle surfaces with no visible segregation or clustering. (g) is a cross-sectional SEM image (printed scale bar 2 μm) of one particle, showing a dense solid interior with a cellular/dendritic solidification network and a distinct outer rim, confirming the powder is neither hollow nor porous. The printed panel letters (a)–(g) do not match the caption, which assigns the element maps to (e)–(h); no numeric composition values are printed on any panel beyond the scale bars.

subfigures.description: Low-magnification SEM image of a large, densely packed powder bed; printed scale bar 400 μm. Nearly all particles are spherical and of similar size, with no satellites or irregular particles apparent. A dashed white box marks the region shown as the inset (b) in the upper-right.

High-magnification SEM image (dashed inset within (a)) of a single powder particle; printed scale bar 10 μm. The surface is smooth and rounded but shows faint granular/faceted contrast; neighbouring spherical particles are visible at the edges.

EDS elemental map labelled "Fe" in the top-right corner, rendered in yellow. Fe signal is spread uniformly over the large central particle and the surrounding particles, with no noticeable enrichment or depletion.
EDS elemental map labelled "Mn" in the top-right corner, rendered in blue. Mn appears homogeneously distributed across the particle, matching the morphology of the SEM image.
EDS elemental map labelled "Al" in the top-right corner, rendered in red. Al distribution is uniform over the particle with no visible clustering or segregation.
EDS elemental map labelled "Ni" in the top-right corner, rendered in magenta. Ni signal is faintly but uniformly distributed across the particle.

Cross-sectional SEM image of a single powder particle; printed scale bar 2 μm. The interior is fully solid and dense, showing a cellular/dendritic solidification network with a distinct darker outer rim; no internal pores or hollow core are visible.

observations.observation: Panel (a) is a low-magnification SEM image of a large powder bed with a printed scale bar of 400 μm; the particles appear highly spherical, closely size-matched and free of satellites or irregular fragments.
Panel (b) is a dashed-box inset within (a) showing a single particle at high magnification with a printed scale bar of 10 μm; its surface is smooth and rounded with faint granular/faceted contrast.
Panel (c) is an EDS map labelled "Fe" in the top-right corner and rendered in yellow, with the Fe signal evenly spread over the mapped particles.
Panel (d) is an EDS map labelled "Mn" rendered in blue, (e) is labelled "Al" rendered in red, and (f) is labelled "Ni" rendered in magenta; each map covers the same particle field as the SEM images.

Panel (g) is a cross-sectional SEM image of one particle with a printed scale bar of 2 μm, showing a solid dense interior with a cellular/dendritic network and a distinct outer rim, i.e. no internal porosity or hollow core.

The printed panel letters in the image run (a)–(g), but the caption assigns the Fe, Mn, Al and Ni EDS maps to (e), (f), (g) and (h) and also calls (g) the cross-sectional image; the image and caption lettering therefore disagree.
The caption states the powder is a PREP-prepared Fe–30Mn–9Al–C–3Ni powder.
The citing text states the PREP-prepared Fe–30Mn–9Al–C–3Ni powder is highly spherical with no satellites or irregular particles observed, as shown in Fig. 2(a) and (b).
The citing text states that Fe, Mn, Al and Ni in the powder are clearly uniformly distributed (Fig. 2(c)–(f)).
The citing text states that the C distribution is not included in the EDS maps because the conductive tape holding the powder contains a large amount of C.
The citing text states that the cross-sectional image of a particle reveals the solid nature of the powder (Fig. 2(g)).

The citing text reports that particles are mainly in the 15–53 μm range with a median particle size (D50) of 35.69 μm and a Hall flowability value of 14 s/50 g, but these values are attributed to Fig. 3 and no such numbers are printed in this figure.
